guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, valid_q is forced to 0 regardless of other inputs.
When en_i is low or clr_i is high (and not in reset), valid_q is forced to 0.
When set_i is high and en_i is high and clr_i is low (and not in reset), valid_q is set to 1.
When en_i is high, clr_i is low, set_i is low, and no reset, valid_q retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: set_i is asserted only when a valid sideload key is actually present and stable.
assumptions.risk: If set_i is spuriously asserted, valid_q will be set, possibly leading to downstream acceptance of an invalid or zeroized key, compromising security.

uncertain_points.claim: valid_q is cleared by !en_i or clr_i, but the actual sideload key data may not be cleared simultaneously; a mismatch can occur where valid=0 while key data remains stale.
uncertain_points.cond: when en_i goes low or clr_i is asserted
uncertain_points.risk: After re-enable, a consumer may see valid=1 but the key data has not been refreshed or is still the old secret, potentially using an unintended key.

uncertain_points.claim: When valid_q is cleared (by reset, !en_i, or clr_i), the associated key storage is not wiped by this chunk; it relies entirely on external logic to clear secret material.
uncertain_points.risk: If external clear of key data is incomplete or omitted, secret key values may persist and be vulnerable to extraction or later misuse.
